subject: Technical synopsis and action grid for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex@neurolytics.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Technical synopsis and action grid for Redwood pilot

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment on requirements and next steps. I tried to separate goals, constraints, and concrete asks so we can move to a pilot scope quickly.

Pain points you shared
- Reranker latency at peak (esp. 512–1k token contexts) causing dropped sessions in live triage flows.
- Cost volatility tied to per-token rerank passes on in-memory context windows.
- Need for structured diagnosis output (JSON) to avoid heavy post-processing on your side.
- Desire to stream partial results to reduce perceived latency in the UI and support early fallback logic.

Primary goals for a 6-week pilot
1) Reduce P95 inference latency for reranking flows to <250ms at target traffic (40–60 qps burstable).
2) Validate streaming + function-calling flow for structured outputs (diagnosis JSON + categorical tags).
3) Demonstrate 30–40% unit-cost improvement via caching + batching + model variant routing.

Technical fit notes (high level)
- We recommend Redwood streaming + function-calling to send partial JSON as it’s generated; server-side function calls will allow you to persist incremental structured results without waiting for final token generation.
- For reranking, we can route to a quantized model variant for low-cost bulk reranks and fallback to a higher-precision variant for top-k candidates.
- KV-cache/prefix caching will substantially reduce repeated context cost for session-based triage.

Immediate action grid (owners & ETA)
- Soojin: Deliver integration-impact matrix + proposed architecture (attached) — EOD Tue 11/17.
- Karthik: Sketch SDK change summary & sample function-calling schema for your QA pipeline — Wed 11/18.
- Marissa: Draft pilot commercial terms + MSA checklist and follow up with procurement contacts — Wed 11/18.
- Alex/Priya: Share sample anonymized data schema and 24-hour traffic profile (CSV) — by Thu 11/19.

Attachments: redwood-proposed-arch.pdf, integration-impact-matrix.xlsx (light-weight; includes estimated token profiles & ops).

Can you confirm the goals above and whether the proposed owners/ETAs work? If yes, we’ll book a 30-min technical kickoff next week (suggest Tue 11/23 or Wed 11/24).

Short signature —
Soojin Lee

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical synopsis and action grid for Redwood pilot

Thanks — adding a few concrete technical points that will affect integration effort and SDK changes. Pasting high-level decisions so Alex & Priya see tradeoffs up front.

1) Function-calling schema - We should define a small, explicit JSON schema for the diagnosis object so the SDK can emit partial objects during streaming. Example: {"case_id": string, "diagnoses": [ {"code": string, "confidence": float, "notes": string } ], "tags": [string], "meta": {}}
Note: we'll push a typed proto + TypeScript interface in the SDK branch.

2) Streaming behavior & checkpoints - Plan: chunked streaming with 128-token flush windows for UI responsiveness; emit a partial JSON when function-call boundary reached. We'll include an incremental state token so Neurolytics can reconcile out-of-order updates.

3) SDK surface changes - Small additions: a streaming-callback hook, function-call auto-deserialization, and a lightweight retry/backoff for transient GPU queuing. Expect ~12–18 dev hours for an initial patch and tests. I attached a diff with the minimum patch set (sdk-patch-diff.patch).

4) Model/quantization approach - Suggest starting with an int8 quantized reranker for bulk passes and a float16 variant for final scoring. We'll run A/B to measure variance in accuracy; initial config will bias toward latency/cost.

5) Security/retention - If Neurolytics needs Private deployment, we can mirror the same APIs with customer-managed KMS. For the pilot, hosted with contract-level retention controls would work; we’ll document the retention TTLs in the MSA.

I can take point on the SDK PR once we have the schema agreed.

—Karthik
Principal Applied Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex@neurolytics.ai>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical synopsis and action grid for Redwood pilot

Hi Soojin / Karthik —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we share the sample data:

1) Data privacy / retention: For the hosted pilot, what is the default retention TTL and can you guarantee that logs can be purged on demand for the pilot window? We may need evidence for our security review.
2) Pilot ROI: Do you have a short template we can use to model the 30–40% unit-cost improvement assumption, ideally with example token profiles?
3) Implementation timeline: Nov 29 start is tight but possible — we’d need a two-week runway on our side to anonymize exports and provision test accounts. Is your suggested tech kickoff on Tue 11/23 still feasible?

Also confirming we’ll share a daily traffic CSV and a sample anonymized messages export by Thu 11/19.

On the streaming/function-calling idea — looks promising. One thought: for safety we’ll want a strict schema validator on the deserialized JSON and a configurable drop-to-fallback option if confidence < X.

Thanks —
Alex Turner
Head of Platform | Neurolytics Inc.

Alex / Priya —

Thanks — answers inline below and next steps.

1) Retention: For hosted pilots we offer a configurable TTL; default is 90 days but we can set a 7–30 day window for the pilot and provide on-demand purge with audit confirmation. I’ll include the retention statement in the MSA draft Marissa will send.

2) ROI template: Attached matrix (integration-impact-matrix.xlsx) has a simple model with token profiles, expected cache hit rates, and cost delta between quantized vs float variants. I’ll also upload a blank ROI workbook to the Drive folder so you can plug your traffic.

3) Timeline & kickoff: Tue 11/23 is tight for our engineering calendar but doable if we lock scope by Fri 11/20. Proposed plan:
- Thu 11/19: Neurolytics sends anonymized sample + traffic CSV.
- Fri 11/20: Redwood confirms final pilot scope (owners/ETA).
- Tue 11/23 11:00am PT: Technical kickoff (30m) — invite sent if that works.

Safety/validation note: Agree on a post-deserialization schema validator; we’ll include a configurable confidence threshold and fallback routing to a conservative model. Karthik will include validator hooks in the SDK patch.

Next immediate ask from you: if you can confirm the anonymization timeline and that sample export will include per-request token counts, we’ll finalize the kickoff invite.

I’ll also share the mutual-action-plan.docx (one-pager) for quick signoff and Marissa will follow up on terms.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—So
